sources: 112: Ministry of Home Affairs (Emergency Response Support System, 112.gov.in). 108: National Health Mission ambulance service, run by each state. Tele-MANAS: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

numbers.label: All emergencies: police, fire and ambulance. Works across India.
Emergency ambulance, available in most states.
Tele-MANAS: free, confidential mental health support, 24/7. Also 1-800-891-4416.

numbers_note: These numbers are for India. If you are in another country, use your local emergency number. If 108 doesn't connect in your area, call 112.

warning_signs.title: Chest pain or pressure
warning_signs.detail: Pain, tightness or pressure in the chest, especially if it spreads to the arm, jaw or back, or comes with sweating or breathlessness.

warning_signs.title: Difficulty breathing
warning_signs.detail: Struggling to breathe, not able to speak in full sentences, or lips turning blue or grey.

warning_signs.title: Signs of a stroke
warning_signs.detail: Face drooping on one side, weakness in an arm or leg, or slurred or confused speech that starts suddenly.

warning_signs.title: Fainting or unresponsiveness
warning_signs.detail: Losing consciousness, not waking up properly, or sudden confusion.

warning_signs.title: Seizure
warning_signs.detail: A fit or seizure, especially a first one or one lasting more than five minutes.

warning_signs.title: Severe bleeding
warning_signs.detail: Bleeding that doesn't stop with firm pressure, or a serious injury.

warning_signs.title: Severe allergic reaction
warning_signs.detail: Swelling of the face, lips or throat, difficulty swallowing, or a rash with breathlessness.

warning_signs.title: Sudden severe headache
warning_signs.detail: The worst headache of your life, or a headache with a stiff neck, high fever or rash.

warning_signs.title: Risk of self-harm
warning_signs.detail: If you or someone else may be at risk of self-harm, get help immediately. You are not alone.

see_doctor_soon: A high fever that doesn't come down, or any fever in a baby under 3 months.
Vomiting or diarrhoea where you can't keep fluids down, or you're passing very little urine.
Symptoms that are getting worse, or haven't improved after a few days.
A new pain, lump or change in your body that worries you.
Feeling unwell if you are pregnant, older, or have a long-term health condition.
while_waiting: Call 112 (or 108 for an ambulance). Say what is happening and exactly where you are.
Stay with the person and keep them as calm and comfortable as you can.
Don't drive yourself to hospital if you have severe symptoms.
Unlock the door and, if possible, ask someone to meet the ambulance.
Keep a list of the person's medicines and allergies ready for the medical team.
everyday_tips: Save 112 and 108 in your phone, and teach children when to use them.
Know where your nearest hospital with an emergency department is.
Keep a written list of your medicines, allergies and health conditions in your wallet or phone.
Keep a basic first-aid kit at home, and check it every few months.
Store medicines, cleaning products and chemicals out of children's reach.
